The Ramblers, led by seventh-year head coach [[Porter Moser]], played their home games at the [[Joseph J. Gentile Arena]] in [[Chicago]]. They were members of the [[Missouri Valley Conference]]. With a win against [[2017–18 Evansville Purple Aces men's basketball team|Evansville]] on February 18, 2018, Loyola clinched at least a share of its first-ever Missouri Valley Conference regular season championship.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400989747|title=Loyola-Chicago vs. Evansville – Game Recap – February 18, 2018 – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-02-19}} With a win over [[2017–18 Southern Illinois Salukis men's basketball team|Southern Illinois]] on February 21, the Ramblers clinched the outright MVC championship.{{Cite news|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-loyola-siu-20180221-story.html|title=Loyola clinches Missouri Valley title with 75–56 win over Southern Illinois|last=Greenstein|first=Teddy|work=chicagotribune.com|access-date=2018-02-22|language=en-US}} The Ramblers defeated [[2017–18 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team|Northern Iowa]], [[2017–18 Bradley Braves men's basketball team|Bradley]], and [[2017–18 Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball team|Illinois State]] to win the [[2018 Missouri Valley Conference men's basketball tournament|MVC tournament]]. As a result, the Ramblers received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As the No. 11 seed in the South Region, they upset No. 6-seeded [[2017–18 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami (FL)]] on a last second three-pointer. In the Second Round, they defeated No. 3-seeded [[2017–18 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] to earn the school's first trip to the Sweet Sixteen since [[1985 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1985]]. They then defeated [[2017–18 Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team|Nevada]] in the Sweet Sixteen and [[2017-18 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]] in the Elite Eight to advance to the Final Four for the first time since [[1963 NCAA University Division basketball tournament|1963]]. Their [[Cinderella (sports)|Cinderella run]] ended with a loss to the eventual runner-up [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] in the national semifinal. The Ramblers' run also made the team's then-98-year-old chaplain [[Jean Dolores Schmidt|Sister Jean]] a national and even international media figure. ==Previous season== The [[2016–17 Loyola Ramblers men's basketball team|Ramblers]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 18–14, 8–10 in [[2016–17 Missouri Valley Conference men's basketball season|MVC play]] to finish in fifth place.
